passages.text: Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and a brother of James, To those who are called, loved by God the Father, and kept in Jesus Christ: Mercy, peace, and love be multiplied to you.
passages.sermon:
Jude writes this letter.
Jude serves Jesus Christ.
Jude is the brother of James.
Jude writes to people who are called by God.
God the Father loves these people.
Jesus Christ keeps these people safe.
Jude prays for mercy for them.
Jude prays for peace for them.
Jude prays for love for them.
Jude asks that mercy, peace, and love increase for them.
passages.original: Ἰούδας Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ δοῦλος ἀδελφὸς δὲ Ἰακώβου Τοῖς ἐν Θεῷ Πατρὶ ἠγαπημένοις καὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ τετηρημένοις κλητοῖς Ἔλεος ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη καὶ ἀγάπη πληθυνθείη

passages.text: Beloved, although I made every effort to write to you about the salvation we share, I felt it necessary to write and urge you to contend earnestly for the faith entrusted once for all to the saints.
passages.sermon:
Jude is a servant of Jesus Christ.
Jude is a brother of James.
Jude writes to those who are called by God.
God the Father loves these people.
Jesus Christ keeps them safe.
Jude calls them "beloved."
Jude tried very hard to write about the salvation they all share.
Jude found it necessary to write for another reason.
Jude urges them to fight for the faith.
God gave this faith to the saints once for all time.
passages.original: Ἀγαπητοί πᾶσαν σπουδὴν ποιούμενος γράφειν ὑμῖν περὶ τῆς κοινῆς ἡμῶν σωτηρίας ἀνάγκην ἔσχον γράψαι ὑμῖν παρακαλῶν ἐπαγωνίζεσθαι τῇ ἅπαξ παραδοθείσῃ τοῖς ἁγίοις πίστει

passages.text: For certain men have crept in among you unnoticed—ungodly ones who were designated long ago for condemnation. They turn the grace of our God into a license for immorality, and they deny our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
Certain men have come in among you secretly.
These men are ungodly.
Long ago, God marked them for condemnation.
They change the grace of our God into a reason for immoral living.
They deny Jesus Christ.
Jesus Christ is our only Master and Lord.
passages.original: παρεισέδυσαν γάρ τινες ἄνθρωποι οἱ πάλαι προγεγραμμένοι εἰς τοῦτο τὸ κρίμα ἀσεβεῖς τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν χάριτα μετατιθέντες εἰς ἀσέλγειαν καὶ τὸν μόνον Δεσπότην καὶ Κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἀρνούμενοι

passages.text: Although you are fully aware of this, I want to remind you that after Jesus had delivered His people out of the land of Egypt, He destroyed those who did not believe.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saved His people from the land of Egypt.
Some people did not believe Him.
Jesus destroyed those who did not believe.
You already know this truth.
I want to remind you of it.
passages.original: Ὑπομνῆσαι δὲ ὑμᾶς βούλομαι εἰδότας ὑμᾶς ἅπαξ πάντα ὅτι Ἰησοῦς λαὸν ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου σώσας τὸ δεύτερον τοὺς μὴ πιστεύσαντας ἀπώλεσεν

passages.text: And the angels who did not stay within their own domain but abandoned their proper dwelling—these He has kept in eternal chains under darkness, bound for judgment on that great day.
passages.sermon:
God acted with justice and power.
Some angels did not remain in their own position of authority.
These angels left their proper dwelling.
God has kept these angels in eternal chains.
He has placed them under darkness.
God holds them there until the judgment of the great day.
passages.original: ἀγγέλους τε τοὺς μὴ τηρήσαντας τὴν ἑαυτῶν ἀρχὴν ἀλλὰ ἀπολιπόντας τὸ ἴδιον οἰκητήριον εἰς κρίσιν μεγάλης ἡμέρας δεσμοῖς ἀϊδίοις ὑπὸ ζόφον τετήρηκεν

passages.text: In like manner, Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities around them, who indulged in sexual immorality and pursued strange flesh, are on display as an example of those who sustain the punishment of eternal fire.
passages.sermon:
Sodom and Gomorrah were two cities.
The cities around them acted in the same way.
These cities practiced sexual immorality.
They pursued unnatural desires.
God punished them with eternal fire.
Their punishment is an example for others.
God uses their fate to warn everyone.
passages.original: ὡς Σόδομα καὶ Γόμορρα καὶ αἱ περὶ αὐτὰς πόλεις τὸν ὅμοιον τρόπον τούτοις ἐκπορνεύσασαι καὶ ἀπελθοῦσαι ὀπίσω σαρκὸς ἑτέρας πρόκεινται δεῖγμα πυρὸς αἰωνίου δίκην ὑπέχουσαι

passages.text: Yet in the same way these dreamers defile their bodies, reject authority, and slander glorious beings.
passages.sermon:
These people are dreamers.
They act in the same way as those who sinned before.
They defile their own bodies.
They reject authority.
They slander glorious beings.
passages.original: Ὁμοίως μέντοι καὶ οὗτοι ἐνυπνιαζόμενοι σάρκα μὲν μιαίνουσιν κυριότητα δὲ ἀθετοῦσιν δόξας δὲ βλασφημοῦσιν

passages.text: But even the archangel Michael, when he disputed with the devil over the body of Moses, did not presume to bring a slanderous charge against him, but said, “The Lord rebuke you!”
passages.sermon:
Michael is an archangel.
Michael argued with the devil.
They argued about the body of Moses.
Michael did not dare to accuse the devil with slander.
Michael did not bring a judgment of blasphemy against the devil.
Michael said, “The Lord rebuke you!”
passages.original: ὁ δὲ Μιχαὴλ ὁ ἀρχάγγελος ὅτε τῷ διαβόλῳ διακρινόμενος διελέγετο περὶ τοῦ Μωϋσέως σώματος οὐκ ἐτόλμησεν κρίσιν ἐπενεγκεῖν βλασφημίας ἀλλὰ εἶπεν Ἐπιτιμήσαι σοι Κύριος

passages.text: These men, however, slander what they do not understand, and like irrational animals, they will be destroyed by the things they do instinctively.
passages.sermon:
These men act without understanding.
They speak evil about things they do not know.
They act by instinct, like irrational animals.
They destroy themselves by the very things they do by nature.
passages.original: οὗτοι δὲ ὅσα μὲν οὐκ οἴδασιν βλασφημοῦσιν ὅσα δὲ φυσικῶς ὡς τὰ ἄλογα ζῷα ἐπίστανται ἐν τούτοις φθείρονται

passages.text: Woe to them! They have traveled the path of Cain; they have rushed headlong into the error of Balaam; they have perished in Korah’s rebellion.
passages.sermon:
These men act in evil ways.
They follow the path of Cain.
Cain killed his brother Abel.
They run after the error of Balaam for money.
Balaam loved reward more than God.
They are destroyed like Korah.
Korah rebelled against God and perished.
Woe to them!
passages.original: οὐαὶ αὐτοῖς ὅτι τῇ ὁδῷ τοῦ Κάϊν ἐπορεύθησαν καὶ τῇ πλάνῃ τοῦ Βαλαὰμ μισθοῦ ἐξεχύθησαν καὶ τῇ ἀντιλογίᾳ τοῦ Κόρε ἀπώλοντο

passages.text: These men are hidden reefs in your love feasts, shamelessly feasting with you but shepherding only themselves. They are clouds without water, carried along by the wind; fruitless trees in autumn, twice dead after being uprooted.
passages.sermon:
These men are dangerous.
They hide among you during your love feasts.
They join your meals without fear.
They care only for themselves.
They do not care for others.
They are like clouds without water.
The wind carries them away.
They are like fruitless trees in autumn.
They do not produce any fruit.
They are twice dead.
They have been uprooted.
passages.original: Οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ ἐν ταῖς ἀγάπαις ὑμῶν σπιλάδες συνευωχούμενοι ἀφόβως ἑαυτοὺς ποιμαίνοντες νεφέλαι ἄνυδροι ὑπὸ ἀνέμων παραφερόμεναι δένδρα φθινοπωρινὰ ἄκαρπα δὶς ἀποθανόντα ἐκριζωθέντα

passages.text: They are wild waves of the sea, foaming up their own shame; wandering stars, for whom blackest darkness has been reserved forever.
passages.sermon:
These men are false teachers.
They act without fear.
They are like wild waves on the sea.
They bring up their own shame like foam.
They are like wandering stars.
God has kept the deepest darkness for them forever.
passages.original: κύματα ἄγρια θαλάσσης ἐπαφρίζοντα τὰς ἑαυτῶν αἰσχύνας ἀστέρες πλανῆται οἷς ὁ ζόφος τοῦ σκότους εἰς αἰῶνα τετήρηται

passages.text: Enoch, the seventh from Adam, also prophesied about them: “Behold, the Lord is coming with myriads of His holy ones to execute judgment on everyone, and to convict all the ungodly of every ungodly act of wickedness and every harsh word spoken against Him by ungodly sinners.”
passages.sermon:
Enoch was the seventh man from Adam.
Enoch prophesied about these men.
Enoch said, “Look, the Lord is coming.
He comes with thousands of His holy ones.
The Lord will judge everyone.
He will convict all the ungodly.
He will show them their ungodly deeds.
They did these wicked things in an ungodly way.
He will also show them every harsh word.
Ungodly sinners spoke these words against Him.”
passages.original: Προεφήτευσεν δὲ καὶ τούτοις ἕβδομος ἀπὸ Ἀδὰμ Ἑνὼχ λέγων Ἰδοὺ ἦλθεν Κύριος ἐν ἁγίαις μυριάσιν αὐτοῦ ποιῆσαι κρίσιν κατὰ πάντων καὶ ἐλέγξαι πάντας τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς περὶ πάντων τῶν ἔργων ἀσεβείας αὐτῶν ὧν ἠσέβησαν καὶ περὶ πάντων τῶν σκληρῶν ὧν ἐλάλησαν κατ’ αὐτοῦ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἀσεβεῖς

passages.text: These men are discontented grumblers, following after their own lusts; their mouths spew arrogance; they flatter others for their own advantage.
passages.sermon:
These men complain.
They are never content.
They follow their own desires.
They speak with arrogance.
They flatter others.
They do this to gain something for themselves.
passages.original: Οὗτοί εἰσιν γογγυσταί μεμψίμοιροι κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας αὐτῶν πορευόμενοι καὶ τὸ στόμα αὐτῶν λαλεῖ ὑπέρογκα θαυμάζοντες πρόσωπα ὠφελείας χάριν

passages.text: But you, beloved, remember what was foretold by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ when they said to you, “In the last times there will be scoffers who will follow after their own ungodly desires.”
passages.sermon:
You are beloved by God.
Remember the words spoken before.
The apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ spoke these words.
They told you what would happen.
They said, “In the last times, there will be scoffers.”
These scoffers will follow their own ungodly desires.
passages.original: Ὑμεῖς δέ ἀγαπητοί μνήσθητε τῶν ῥημάτων τῶν προειρημένων ὑπὸ τῶν ἀποστόλων τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ὅτι ἔλεγον ὑμῖν Ἐπ’ ἐσχάτου τοῦ χρόνου ἔσονται ἐμπαῖκται κατὰ τὰς ἑαυτῶν ἐπιθυμίας πορευόμενοι τῶν ἀσεβειῶν

passages.text: These are the ones who cause divisions, who are worldly and devoid of the Spirit.
passages.sermon: These people cause divisions.\r\nThey are worldly.\r\nThey do not have the Spirit.
passages.original: Οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ ἀποδιορίζοντες ψυχικοί Πνεῦμα μὴ ἔχοντες

passages.text: But you, beloved, by building yourselves up in your most holy faith and praying in the Holy Spirit, keep yourselves in the love of God as you await the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ to bring you eternal life.
passages.sermon:
You are beloved by God.
You must build yourselves up in your most holy faith.
You must pray in the Holy Spirit.
You must keep yourselves in the love of God.
You must wait for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ.
This mercy will bring you eternal life.
passages.original: Ὑμεῖς δέ ἀγαπητοί ἐποικοδομοῦντες ἑαυτοὺς τῇ ἁγιωτάτῃ ὑμῶν πίστει ἐν Πνεύματι Ἁγίῳ προσευχόμενοι ἑαυτοὺς ἐν ἀγάπῃ Θεοῦ τηρήσατε προσδεχόμενοι τὸ ἔλεος τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον

passages.text: And indeed, have mercy on those who doubt; save others by snatching them from the fire; and to still others show mercy tempered with fear, hating even the clothing stained by the flesh.
passages.sermon:
Show mercy to people who doubt.
Rescue others from danger.
Pull them out of the fire.
Show mercy to others, but do it with fear.
Hate even the clothing that is stained by sinful actions.
passages.original: Καὶ οὓς μὲν ἐλεᾶτε διακρινομένους οὓς δὲ σῴζετε ἐκ πυρὸς ἁρπάζοντες οὓς δὲ ἐλεᾶτε ἐν φόβῳ μισοῦντες καὶ τὸν ἀπὸ τῆς σαρκὸς ἐσπιλωμένον χιτῶνα

passages.text: Now to Him who is able to keep you from stumbling and to present you unblemished in His glorious presence, with great joy— to the only God our Savior be glory, majesty, dominion, and authority through Jesus Christ our Lord before all time, and now, and for all eternity. Amen.
passages.sermon:
God is our only Savior.
God can keep you from stumbling.
God can make you stand without fault.
God can bring you into His glorious presence.
God gives you great joy.
Jesus Christ is our Lord.
God deserves glory.
God deserves majesty.
God deserves power.
God deserves authority.
God deserves these things through Jesus Christ.
God deserves them before all time.
God deserves them now.
God deserves them forever.
Amen.
passages.original: Τῷ δὲ δυναμένῳ φυλάξαι ὑμᾶς ἀπταίστους καὶ στῆσαι κατενώπιον τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ ἀμώμους ἐν ἀγαλλιάσει μόνῳ Θεῷ Σωτῆρι ἡμῶν διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν δόξα μεγαλωσύνη κράτος καὶ ἐξουσία πρὸ παντὸς τοῦ αἰῶνος καὶ νῦν καὶ εἰς πάντας τοὺς αἰῶνας Ἀμήν
